chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, he should bear witness to that. When three menstrual periods have passed from that day, her waiting period (iddah) is completed.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This ruling is valid for her only if clear evidence establishes that he divorced her on a specific day. If such evidence does not establish that, she should observe the waiting period from the day the news reaches her, indicating that.
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period calculated for a wife when her husband divorces her while he is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the commencement of the waiting period (iddah) for a wife whose husband is absent, distinguishing between scenarios where the specific day of divorce is proven versus when it is merely reported. Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that if evidence confirms the exact day of divorce, the iddah begins from that day; otherwise, it starts from the day the news reaches her, a ruling refined by Imam al-Hasan (AS) to emphasize the necessity of clear testimony. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on evidentiary certainty in personal status law to prevent uncertainty in marital obligations.
